goal: ship a deep, checkable OR tool: job shop scheduling with a proved bound, benchmarked honestly against the standard instances
notes: Idea: job-shop-scheduler (explore). Engine: GT dispatch rules, N5 tabu search with Taillard estimate, preemptive one-machine bound, B&B on <=64 ops. Benchmark at 4 s/instance on all 162 JSPLIB instances: 66 of 103 recorded optima matched, 54 of 162 proved, mean gap 1.01%, 0 below a recorded lower bound; ta29 below JSPLIB's dated UB but not the published best (said so on every surface). The small-instance rows (N<=64) were re-run after a final change to the tabu time slice and are identical. Local verification: run_venture_tests.py job-shop-scheduler assembly-line-balancer ok; run_workflow_locally --for-changes: every run step passed, test/Test the site builder timed out locally (no verdict) and passed in CI. GitHub CI: all check runs green on the head before the record commit. Data not vendored (JSPLIB has no licence).

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured
